note: White-box inspection performed by the ValidateHE orchestrator (Claude Fable) after the dispatched white-box subagent was cut off by a session limit before writing findings. Line-by-line inspection of critical calculations plus root-causing of the black-box failures, on the read-only scratch copy; no model files were modified.

findings.test: Root cause of BB-PSM-ORD: OS >= PFS ordering not guaranteed on extrapolation
findings.target: OS/PFS parametric survival fitting and prediction
findings.inputs: 04_parametric_survival_analysis.R best-fit selection; model_fun.R partition construction; black-box BB-PSM-ORD (PFS>OS over ~49-51% of the 10y horizon for crp+ and tmb_braf+ subgroups)
findings.expected: OS(t) >= PFS(t) at every time point by construction, so the post-progression state P = OS - PFS is well-defined over the whole horizon
findings.observed: OS and PFS are fit as SEPARATE parametric models, each independently choosing its own best-fit distribution by AIC (find_best_model(os_ic,'AIC') and find_best_model(pfs_ic,'AIC'), 04_parametric_survival_analysis.R:155-156; candidate set exponential/weibull/weibullph/llogis/lognormal/gamma/gompertz/gengamma/genf at 06:104-105). Nothing constrains the two fitted/extrapolated curves to preserve OS>=PFS. The black-box confirmed PFS exceeds OS across roughly half the extrapolated horizon for treated subgroups (not just near t=0). Because model_fun then does p_p = pmax(os - pfs, 0) after clamping pfs to os, the progressed state is forced to ZERO occupancy for that entire span -- i.e. the model asserts no post-progression time over ~50% of the horizon for biomarker-positive arms. Post-progression utility (u_p) and follow-up/end-of-life costs differ from progression-free, so this materially distorts the QALY/cost partition of the treated arms and therefore the incremental results.
findings.recommended_fix: Do not fit OS and PFS as unconstrained independent models. Options: (a) jointly model or fit a single distribution family constrained so extrapolated OS>=PFS; (b) model PFS and the PFS->OS gap (post-progression survival) separately and reconstruct OS=PFS+gap so ordering holds by construction; (c) at minimum, elevate the pmin() event from a warning() to a hard diagnostic that reports the fraction of the horizon affected, and add the partition distortion to the limitations. Quantify the QALY/cost impact of the clamp before publishing.

findings.test: Documented distribution vs implemented distribution selection
findings.inputs: Manuscript methods ('Gamma distributions were selected for both endpoints and applied consistently') vs 04_parametric_survival_analysis.R best-fit-by-AIC logic
findings.expected: The distribution family used by the deployed model matches the one described in the documentation
findings.observed: The manuscript states gamma was selected for both PFS and OS, but the code selects the best model per endpoint by AIC over a 9-distribution candidate set (06:104-105,155-156). If AIC does not pick gamma for both, the deployed extrapolations differ from the documented ones; the black-box empirically observed OS behaving Weibull-like and PFS lognormal-like, which if correct contradicts the 'gamma for both' claim and is itself a driver of the crossing in WB-001.
findings.recommended_fix: Either hard-code the documented gamma family (if that is the intended, reviewed choice) or update the documentation to state that distributions are auto-selected by AIC per endpoint and report which were actually chosen. Reconcile with the manuscript's 'gamma for both' statement.

findings.test: Error-masking: PFS>OS crossing suppressed to a warning and silently clamped
findings.inputs: model_fun.R:306-312 (control) and 375-382 (biomarker): if(any(pfs>os)) warning(...); pfs <- pmin(pfs, os)
findings.expected: A structural violation of OS>=PFS should surface as an actionable diagnostic, not be silently corrected
findings.observed: The crossing is handled with a warning() (easily lost in a batch/PSA run) followed by pmin() that changes the partition. In deterministic base-case runs this masks the WB-001 mis-fit; in PSA it is expected to fire frequently. The magnitude (fraction of horizon clamped, resulting QALY shift) is neither reported nor bounded.
findings.recommended_fix: Fix the ordering at the source (WB-001). While the clamp remains, record the clamped fraction and the QALY/cost delta per strategy and per PSA iteration so the distortion is auditable rather than hidden.

findings.test: Root cause of BB-SW cost-swap failure: diagnostic-test cost keyed to biomarker name string
findings.inputs: calculate_outcomes.R:47-53 (test_costs[1] += c_test_NGS if biomarker=='tmb_braf'; += c_test_blood if biomarker=='crp')
findings.expected: A strategy's diagnostic-test cost should follow the strategy's data/definition, so that swapping two strategies' inputs swaps their costs too
findings.observed: The NGS (TMB/BRAF) and extra CRP test costs are attached by matching the biomarker NAME STRING, not by any data carried with the strategy. Swapping the crp and tmb_braf curve data (black-box BB-SW) correctly swapped QALYs/LYs but NOT costs, because the name-keyed cost stayed put. Correct for the current fixed strategy set, but a latent coupling: any rename/reorder/addition of biomarker strategies silently misassigns diagnostic costs.
findings.recommended_fix: Carry each strategy's diagnostic-test cost as a data field on the strategy/parameter object (e.g. a per-strategy c_test vector) rather than branching on a hard-coded biomarker name, so cost travels with the strategy definition.

findings.test: Root cause of BB-PSM-WCHECK: prevalence drift between CEA weighting and precomputed weighted curves
findings.inputs: 03_biomarker_strategies.R:24-26 p_crp<-mean(data$crp), p_tmb_braf<-mean(data$tmb_braf) (full data, ~74); vs the *_weighted_OS/PFS curves in l_params_base built by population-averaging over data_complete (~68) in prediction_functions/07
findings.expected: A single, consistent biomarker prevalence used everywhere it enters the economics
findings.observed: model_fun's deterministic path weights pos/neg subgroups with p_crp/p_tmb_braf from full `data`, while the precomputed crp_weighted_*/tmb_braf_weighted_* curves (read directly by biomarker_decomposition.qmd) are marginalized over the smaller data_complete cohort. Drift measured by black-box: 0.02pp (CRP), 0.81pp (TMB/BRAF). The CEA itself uses the pos/neg + p_* path, so the base-case ICERs are internally consistent; the weighted-curve fields are a duplicate representation that can drift and is consumed by a report.
findings.recommended_fix: Compute prevalence once from a single cohort definition and derive both the pos/neg weighting and the *_weighted_* curves from it, or drop the precomputed weighted curves and marginalize on demand using the same p_* values.

findings.inputs: model_fun.R:282-284 v_dw_c<-1/(1+dr_costs)^(seq(0,time_horizon)/52); v_dw_e analogously; calculate_outcomes.R:31,75 per-cycle undiscounted value * v_dw then summed
findings.expected: Per-year discount rate correctly converted to weekly cycles; cycle-0 weight 1; applied to per-cycle streams then summed
findings.observed: Correct. The exponent (cycle index)/52 converts weekly cycle number to years, so the annual rate dr is applied as (1+dr)^(-t_years); cycle 0 gets weight 1; the weight vector multiplies the per-cycle undiscounted cost/QALY streams and is then summed. No naive r*t and no annual-probability/12 error. Costs and effects use dr_costs and dr_effects symmetrically. Black-box BB-D0 (r=0 -> disc==undisc) and BB-D1 (r up -> totals fall) passed, consistent with this.

findings.test: State-occupancy partition sums to 1 by construction
findings.expected: PF + P + D == 1 at every cycle
findings.observed: By construction PF+P+D = pfs + (os-pfs) + (1-os) = 1 whenever pfs<=os (guaranteed by the preceding pmin clamp). Black-box cohort-conservation checks (BB-TR1) passed for all strategies. The partition identity itself is sound; the concern is that it is achieved via the WB-001/WB-003 clamp rather than by correctly ordered curves.

findings.test: Absence of half-cycle correction; endpoint over-count on the occupancy sum
findings.target: calculate_outcomes.R QALY/LY accumulation over 521 grid points
findings.inputs: time_horizon=520 -> seq(0,520) is 521 points; per-cycle value * cl(=1/52) summed; black-box BB-M0 found undisc LY ~10.019y vs 10y expected (~0.19% high), equal across arms
findings.expected: Undiscounted life-years under mortality=0 equal the 10-year horizon exactly
findings.observed: Summing occupancy at all 521 time points each weighted by cl=1/52 yields 521/52 = 10.019 years, a left-Riemann-sum over-count of about one cycle with no half-cycle correction. The bias is small (~0.19%), systematic, and equal across strategies, so it is ICER-neutral, but it inflates all absolute LY/QALY (and cost streams tied to occupancy) by ~one cycle.
findings.recommended_fix: Apply a half-cycle correction (or trapezoidal integration / endpoint weighting of 0.5) to the occupancy sums, or document the ~0.19% absolute over-count as an accepted approximation given the weekly cycle length.

findings.test: Forward and backward trace of essential calculations
findings.inputs: Forward: u_p (0.59 at UTILITY_SOURCE=1) and c_drug_nivo -> outputs. Backward: total Effect and total Cost -> inputs
findings.expected: Two chosen inputs propagate to the totals, and the totals decompose back into named input components
findings.observed: Forward: u_p enters qalys_p = p_p*u_p*cl (calculate_outcomes.R:29), discounted by v_dw_e and summed into qalys_total -> Effect. c_drug_nivo enters drug_costs = (l_nivo*c_drug_nivo + l_FLOX_exp*c_drug_FLOX)*p_pf for the experimental arm (line 37), discounted and summed into costs_total -> Cost. Backward: Effect = sum_t (p_pf*u_np + p_p*u_p)*cl*v_dw_e; Cost = sum_t (drug+test+visit+follow_up+end_life)*v_dw_c -- both fully decomposable into the returned component streams (qalys_pf/qalys_p, drug_costs/test_costs/visit_costs/follow_up_costs/end_life_costs). Traceability is clean and the returned component lists make it auditable.

findings.test: Treatment and monitoring costs accrue only to progression-free occupancy
findings.inputs: calculate_outcomes.R:37,40,44,56 drug/test/visit costs all multiplied by p_pf (progression-free); follow_up by p_p; end_life by death transitions
findings.expected: Cost accrual weighting matches the intended care pathway
findings.observed: Active treatment, CT/blood testing, and visit costs are applied only to the progression-free fraction (x p_pf); post-progression incurs only follow_up (x p_p) and one-off end-of-life costs. This is a defensible modeling choice (treatment stops at progression) but should be an explicitly documented assumption, since it means no active-treatment or monitoring cost is attributed to progressed patients at all.
findings.recommended_fix: Document the assumption that treatment/monitoring costs cease at progression and that progressed patients incur only follow-up and end-of-life costs; confirm this matches the intended Norwegian care pathway.

findings.test: Hidden-state / error-masking in the PSA fallback path
findings.inputs: model_fun.R:236-259 tryCatch around resampled-curve prediction; warning()+fallback_used<<-TRUE substitutes base-case curves on NA/NULL/error; returned via a fallback_used attribute
findings.expected: A failed PSA iteration must be detectable and excluded, not silently blended with a different estimation method
findings.observed: On prediction failure the code falls back to base-case curves and records fallback_used via <<- for the enclosing scope and a returned attribute (Issue #79). This is a reasonable design, but correctness depends on EVERY caller (10_PSA.R etc.) checking the attribute and replacing fallen-back iterations; a caller that ignores it would mix base-case and resampled draws, understating uncertainty. The black-box PSA batch (100 iters) showed 0% fallback at n=100, so the path was not exercised here -- latent, not active.
findings.recommended_fix: Ensure the PSA driver hard-checks the fallback_used attribute and discards/replaces fallen-back iterations (verify 10_PSA.R does so); consider failing loudly above a fallback-rate threshold rather than silently substituting.

findings.test: flexsurvreg survival prediction returns survival probabilities (not hazard/cumhaz)
findings.inputs: prediction_functions.R population-averaged prediction; curves consumed as S(t) in [0,1] by model_fun
findings.expected: Predicted curves are survival probabilities in [0,1], non-increasing where claimed
findings.observed: Black-box BB-PSM-PFS/OS bounds+monotonicity passed for all strategies (curves in [0,1], non-increasing), consistent with the predictions being survival functions. Individual-curve monotonicity holds; the failure is purely the OS-vs-PFS cross-curve ordering (WB-001), not a within-curve hazard/survival confusion. Full line-level confirmation of the flexsurvreg shape/scale extraction was not exhaustively re-derived here (the dispatched deep-inspection subagent was cut off); the empirical bounds/monotonicity evidence supports correct survival-scale usage.
